A logo and some motion.

Four logos and four animations for the landing page. Open “On the page” to see any of them on the real page; the bar on top switches between them.

Logos

Each one at full size, in the navigation bar, as the browser tab icon, on dark, and down to 16 pixels.

Motion

A and B move the top of the page. C and D move the rest as you scroll. You can pick one of each.

A

Chat plays out

Top of the page · once, when it opens

  1. Your prompt slides up into the chat. It and the Copy button are there from the start.
  2. The agent types, then asks what the project is about.
  3. “My career” gets picked, and the agent answers.
  4. The iPhone slides in from the right with the finished dashboard.

About 4 seconds. Tells the whole story before anyone reads a word.

B

Dashboards slide

Top of the page · keeps going

  1. The iPhone slides between Maya’s year, her money and her health.
  2. The chosen answer in the chat follows: My career, Money, Health.
  3. Click an answer to jump to it. It pauses while your mouse is over it.

Every 3 seconds. Shows that one kit fits any project. On phones the iPhone is hidden, so only the answers change.

C

Reveal on scroll

Every section below the top · once each

  1. Headlines and pictures slide up into place as you reach them.
  2. Cards come in one after another; the diagram slides in from the right.
  3. The line through the five setup steps draws itself.

Calm and familiar, the way Apple product pages move.

D

Follow the scroll

Timeline, examples and steps · tied to your scrolling

  1. The timeline starts close on the countdown cards and zooms out to the whole year.
  2. The three example cards slide in from the right.
  3. The setup steps fill up one by one as you scroll past them.

Scroll back up and it plays backwards. The most playful of the four.

Good to know: the navigation logo grows from 22 to 24 pixels so its lines land on whole pixels on Retina screens. On the live site, the motion stays off for visitors whose device asks for reduced motion.

How the pieces fit.

One Google Sheet holds everything. Every other piece reads from it or writes to it.

The sheet
One Google Sheet in your own Drive. The single source of truth.
Your AI agent
Claude Code or Codex. It builds everything and keeps it working.
The website
Your private dashboard, behind a login. A public page and CV if you want them.
Your chat assistant
The one you already talk to. Tell it what happened; it updates the sheet.
ConnectorsOptional
Email, calendar and other apps that send facts in.

Made for whatever you’re working on.

A career move, your money, your health. All three examples are live: click around.

Career

Maya applies to residency.

Rotations, papers and a shortlist of programs. Plus a public page and a CV.

DashboardPublic page
Money

Pay off the car. Then move out.

A car loan, an emergency fund, monthly bills and the tax return.

Money dashboard
Health

Check-ups, results, a 10 km race.

Appointments to book, lab results over time and a training plan.

Health dashboard

Maya Lindqvist is fictional. Every name, school, hospital and date in her examples is made up. Her dashboard is open so you can try it; yours sits behind a login.

You talk. Your agent builds.

It asks one thing at a time, shows you options to pick from, and explains anything you need to click.

  1. 30 min

    Talk

    Your goals, deadlines and papers, in your own words.

  2. 20–30 min

    Choose

    Click through a few designs, starting from Maya’s.

  3. 15 min

    Store

    One spreadsheet in your Drive. Edit it any time.

  4. 15 min

    Publish

    Your dashboard goes online, behind a login.

  5. 20 min

    Hand off

    Your chat assistant learns your sheet. Then you just tell it what happened.

About two hours in total, over a few days. You can stop after any step.

Free to run.

Free plans and open source. Your agent asks before anything that costs money.

What you need

  • An AI agent that can run commandsClaude Code or Codex, for example.
  • A Google accountYour sheet lives in your own Drive.
  • About two hoursOne conversation, a few choices, two logins.
  • A Cloudflare accountOptional and free. It puts your sites online.

What it costs

  • The kitFree, open source
  • Google DriveFree
  • Hosting on CloudflareFree plan
  • Your own web addressOptional, about $10–15 a year
  • Your AI agentWhat you already pay

Private by design.

Your data stays in your own accounts, in a spreadsheet you can read. Nothing is locked in.

  • Behind a login.Only the emails you allow can open your dashboard.
  • In your Drive.Your sheet, your folders. Nothing in anyone else’s account.
  • Off the public page.Health, money, phone number and address never appear on it.
  • Only real facts.Your agent never guesses. What you don’t know stays empty.
